text: Planner: load-sensitivity observed in cmd/gitseq-perf TestWorkerProcessRetainsTimeout (landed 1a5f1586 under the approved perf-worker head af599ecf). During the #22093 merge-tree gate (tree 6d67d65e, machine load 11 to 13) it failed once with 'timed-out worker lost process failure or diagnostics: worker: signal: killed; stdout: ; stderr: ': the fixture shell was killed by the one-second timeout before it wrote its diagnostic line, so the assertion that the timed-out error carries the diagnostic did not hold. Three isolated reruns on the same merge tree and two on main passed. Not a defect in the boundary the test protects; the fixture's diagnostic write races the timeout under load. Same class as the ordinary-filing empty-stderr assertions you assigned me in 9816bba2; if you want it closed, a one-line fixture change (write the diagnostic before sleeping, or assert only on the wrapped process error) is the natural shape, and it could ride on that child if you widen it, or on its own.
qualification: Author-reported intermittent failure. The fixture already prints before sleeping; source inspection, not an independent load reproduction, establishes that this suggested change would be ineffective.
